thread:
devon: Customer reports chat stream halts after ~120 tokens; sometimes continues after ~20-40s, sometimes not. They're running SSE via a Cloudflare Worker in front of their app. They see HTTP/1.1 200 OK then no further SSE data lines. Asking for repro info and request ids.
customer-support: Can you DM org id and failing request ids? We need x-rdw-request-id to pull traces.
ingrid: Check client logs for x-rdw-request-id or SDK debug logs.
customer-support: DM'ed two ids: req_01H3K4L5M6N7O8P9Q0R1, req_01H3K4L6M6N7O8P9Q0S2. Region: us-west-2. Client says connection remains open but SSE `data:` events stop for ~20s.
alex: Ask customer to run curl streaming with -N -v to capture headers and raw SSE. Send this example:

```
curl -N -v
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}'
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream"
```

Request full -v output and any HAR from browser.
customer-support: Sent curl snippet and asked for curl output, HAR, and any proxy logs.
devon: Also grab proxy/CF worker logs and cf-ray id. Ask if they can reproduce direct from laptop (no proxy) to rule out edge.
tim_ops: Note: CF Workers that combine streaming with resp transforms or enable gzip can coalesce chunks. Recommend pcap or mitmproxy capture.
ingrid: Also request full response headers. We expect Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8, Connection: keep-alive. If Content-Encoding: gzip is present at edge, that's suspicious.
customer-support: Customer returned curl -v and HAR. Curl shows 200 OK and expected headers. After a couple `: ping` comments there's a long silence. They attached a pcap showing TCP-level keepalives but no application payload during the gap. They included cf-ray: 79b2c4d5e6f-SEA.
alex: Please upload pcap and curl output to debug bundle. Request checklist:
- failing request ids (we have them)
- full curl -N -v output
- browser HAR
- pcap or mitmproxy trace
- CF Worker stderr logs and access logs
- client clock/timezone
- whether client used HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1

Ask them to share via S3 link.
customer-support: Bundle uploaded: https://s3.amazonaws.com/customer-dumps/rdw-debug/edge-streaming-2026-03-15.zip
devon: Downloaded. Pcap shows application data stops at 2026-03-15T12:34:28Z and small resume at 12:34:59Z matching their report.
ingrid: Eng-runtime, can you grep for req_01H3K4L5M6N7O8P9Q0R1?
alex: Found internal trace id trace-rt-7d9c. Runtime logs show tokens up to 118 emitted, then an ~31s gap, then final flush. No internal errors or GPU stalls. Likely intermediate buffering/coalescing at edge.
support-bot: @ops-tim assigned incident#4821 to investigate edge buffering.
tim_ops: Asked customer for worker script. Also requested CF logs for cf-ray.
devon: Short-term mitigation: suggest client-side keepalive handler to detect silence and reconnect, or we can temporarily increase server-side SSE keepalive to `: ping` every 3s for that org while investigating.
ingrid: Alex, does runtime currently send keepalive pings? If so, at what interval?
alex: Runtime pings every ~10s. In this trace pings at 0s and 9s were visible, then coalesced by CF before next flush. Reproducing with a CF Worker that forwards streaming and enables compression should reproduce coalescing.
devon: Actions:
- Customer to test direct curl without CF Worker and report
- Customer to share worker script; CF team to check for Response modifications/transformStreams
- Ops to pull CF worker logs for the cf-ray id and check edge compression
- Eng to consider emitting more frequent SSE comments (3s) and doc guidance for CF Workers

customer-support: Shared plan with customer. They'll test direct curl in ~30m and will DM if new request ids appear.
alex: I'll spin up a local CF Worker to reproduce and report back. Keeping thread open until resolved. :thumbsup:
